mainEntity.name: Can I leave a cracked tooth untreated if it doesn't hurt?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even if a cracked tooth is not causing pain, it is generally advisable to have it assessed by a dentist. Some cracks progress silently, and a fracture that causes no symptoms today may worsen over time, potentially leading to more complex treatment needs. A dental examination can help determine whether the crack requires intervention or monitoring. The absence of pain does not necessarily indicate the absence of a problem, so professional evaluation remains the most reliable approach.

mainEntity.name: How is a cracked tooth diagnosed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Diagnosing a cracked tooth typically involves a combination of a detailed patient history, visual examination, probing of the tooth and gum, dental X-rays, and occasionally specialist diagnostic tests such as biting on a stick or the use of a dye to make cracks more visible. Some cracks, particularly vertical root fractures, can be particularly difficult to detect and may require advanced imaging in certain cases. This is why a thorough clinical assessment is essential.

mainEntity.name: Is a cracked tooth a dental emergency?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether a cracked tooth constitutes a dental emergency depends on the symptoms and circumstances. If you are experiencing severe pain, significant swelling, signs of infection (such as a fever or difficulty swallowing), or trauma that has caused a tooth to break significantly, you should seek dental assessment without delay. For minor chips or cracks that are causing mild or no symptoms, a routine appointment may be appropriate — though it is always sensible to contact your dental practice to discuss your specific situation.

mainEntity.name: Can a dental crown save a cracked tooth?

acceptedAnswer.text: In many cases, a dental crown can protect a cracked tooth and prevent the fracture from worsening, particularly when the crack has not extended into the root or pulp. However, outcomes cannot be guaranteed in every case, and the suitability of this treatment depends on the extent of the crack and the overall health of the tooth. Your dentist will assess the situation clinically before recommending a course of action and will discuss the likely outcomes with you.

mainEntity.name: Will a cracked tooth always need a root canal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not all cracked teeth require root canal treatment. Whether root canal treatment is needed depends on whether the crack has affected or compromised the dental pulp — the soft tissue at the centre of the tooth. Superficial cracks that do not reach the pulp can often be managed without root canal treatment. Your dentist will assess the extent of the crack during examination and advise on the most appropriate treatment for your situation.

mainEntity.name: How long can I wait before seeing a dentist about a cracked tooth?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you are experiencing significant pain, swelling, or other concerning symptoms, it is advisable to seek dental advice as soon as possible rather than waiting. For minor chips or cracks with no associated discomfort, a routine appointment is appropriate, though it is still worth arranging this in a timely manner rather than leaving it indefinitely. Delays in assessment can sometimes allow a crack to worsen or infection to develop, which may make treatment more complex. When in doubt, contacting your dental practice to describe your symptoms is always a sensible starting point.
